title: How to Collect References and Examples for Any Creative Project
h1: How to collect references and examples for any creative project
description: How to gather and explain references for designers, writers, video editors and musicians: what to collect, how to annotate it and how to avoid copying.
intro: Words like modern, clean, bold or friendly mean different things to different people. References, meaning examples of work you like, close that gap faster than any description. Yet many buyers either send no references or send a pile of images with no explanation. Good references are chosen with a purpose and annotated so the freelancer understands exactly what you like. This article explains how to collect and present references for any creative project.

faq.q: How many references should I send?
faq.a: Usually three to six well-chosen examples with notes work better than dozens without explanation.

faq.q: Should I include things I dislike?
faq.a: Yes. One or two examples of what to avoid are often very helpful.

faq.q: Is it fine to ask for a copy of a reference?
faq.a: No. References guide direction; the result should be original work.
Competitors, brands you admire, design galleries, your own past work and everyday objects.

faq.q: What if I do not know what I like?
faq.a: Collect widely, then look for patterns in what you chose. A freelancer can help interpret them.
